title: census.py run without --resume detects into factdiff-<date>-N.csv once factdiff-<date>.csv exists, then applies the old log
goal: census.py run's detect step names the log it later applies, summarises and commits, so a rerun of a census date detects, applies and commits one log whichever detect logs of that date exist

run: import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "_tools"); import census; sys.exit(0 if "--out" in census.plan_run("public", "2026-01-01", False, lambda p: True, lambda l, d: False)[0]["argv"] else 1)

clauses.clause: census.py run's detect step names the log it later applies, summarises and commits, so a rerun of a census date detects, applies and commits one log whichever detect logs of that date exist

gates.question: Which detect log does census.py run --resume continue with when several factdiff-<date>[-N].csv exist, and how many names does run_log tell apart?
options: the last existing log of the date, names -2 to -99
gates.recommendation: the last existing log of the date, names -2 to -99
gates.reason: it is the log the run being continued wrote, and the default detect name sequence is the same
gates.answer: the last existing log of the date, names -2 to -99

notes: Regression of BG-gt4egejo (landed in SP-2cq2hse4); premise: the repro exits 1 on origin/main.
